item.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries for House speaker
item.description: US Democrats on Wednesday elected Hakeem Jeffries as their leader and nominee for Speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on course to become the first Black politician to occupy the powerful position. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 votes cast against his nomination, according to US media reports. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressive lawmakers exposed divisions within the Democratic Party over how to exercise its newfound power following a sweeping midterm election victory. His nomination positions him to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as the party prepares to reverse Republican policies and launch investigations into the administration. However, Jeffries must still secure a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3. With Democrats holding a large majority, his election is widely expected to be a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s leadership election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination by acclamation, a process that would have allowed the party to endorse him without a formal ballot. He argued that every Democrat should have the opportunity to assess his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. Although the overall voting figures were made public, individual ballots remained secret. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met with progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare. Proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand healthcare coverage were among the issues considered. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to his party’s governing agenda following the Republican defeat, amid voter dissatisfaction over the Iran war and rising fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters on Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” Brooklyn roots Raised in the working-class Crown Heights neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York State Legislature in 2007. He was elected to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and frequent references to hip-hop artists, he made history in 2022 when Democrats elected him to succeed Nancy Pelosi as their House leader, making him the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress. item.title: Convoy attack: WoPU hails Tinubu over clemency to 78 suspects
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Working People United (WoPU) has commended President Bola Tinubu for granting clemency to the 78 individuals arrested in connection with the attack on his presidential convoy in Abuja, describing the decision as an act of statesmanship, magnanimity and compassionate leadership. In a statement by its National Coordinator-General, Prince Williams Akporeha, the group said the President’s decision demonstrated his commitment to national unity, reconciliation and peace despite the gravity of the incident. WoPU said the gesture reflected Tinubu’s willingness to prioritise forgiveness and national harmony over confrontation. According to the statement, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has once again demonstrated the depth of his compassion, fatherly disposition, and unwavering commitment to the welfare of all Nigerians. “By extending clemency to the 78 suspects arrested over the attack on his convoy, the President has shown that leadership is not merely about the exercise of authority but also about mercy, understanding, and the pursuit of national harmony.” The group described the decision as a demonstration of the President’s belief in second chances and peaceful coexistence, adding that it would help prevent the incident from deepening divisions in the country. WoPU said the gesture was consistent with the objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which seeks to build an inclusive, prosperous and stable Nigeria. It urged Nigerian youths to emulate the President’s example by embracing dialogue, patience and responsible civic engagement. The movement also cautioned young people against allowing themselves to be used by individuals or groups seeking to promote violence and instability for political interests. “It is imperative for Nigerian youths to remain vigilant and responsible. They must resist every attempt by unscrupulous elements to use them as instruments of violence, lawlessness, and political disruption. “The future of our nation lies in peaceful participation, constructive engagement, and unwavering faith in democratic institutions,” the statement added. The group also urged youths to appreciate the administration’s policies and reforms, which it said were designed to promote long-term economic growth, social stability and national development. It reaffirmed its support for the Tinubu administration’s reforms and developmental initiatives, expressing confidence that the Renewed Hope Agenda would deliver positive outcomes for workers, entrepreneurs, artisans, professionals and other Nigerians. WoPU, a civic and socio-political movement comprising workers, traders, artisans, professionals, entrepreneurs and grassroots stakeholders across the country, said it would continue to mobilise support for the President’s vision of a prosperous and united Nigeria beyond 2027. item.title: Reps demand NNPCL accountability, warn on PIA implementation
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stronger accountability in the petroleum sector, warning that poor implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) could undermine the reforms intended to transform the industry. The House said the success of the reforms would depend on transparency, institutional discipline and responsible corporate governance. The position was reinforced at a conference on PIA implementation organised by the House in collaboration with the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and other partners in Abuja. Speaking after the conference, Deputy Spokesman of the House, Philip Agbese, commended NNPCL Group Chief Executive Officer, Bayo Ojulari, for promoting transparency and constructive engagement with the National Assembly. Agbese, a Labour Party member representing a constituency in Benue State, said engagement between the legislature and the national oil company was necessary to ensure that the objectives of the PIA translated into measurable improvements in the petroleum industry. He urged other government agencies to adopt similar open-door approaches in their dealings with the legislature, stressing that transparency and institutional collaboration were essential to effective governance. The conference, themed, “Petroleum Industry Act Implementation: The PIA, Corporate Governance and Legislative Oversight,” was organised in collaboration with the Office of the Speaker of the House, Rep. Abbas Tajudeen. Declaring the conference open, Abbas, who was represented by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere, said the PIA was designed to establish a transparent, commercially viable, accountable and investment-friendly petroleum industry. He, however, warned that the enactment of the law alone would not guarantee the desired reforms without effective implementation. The Speaker said the transformation of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation into a commercially oriented company, the establishment of independent regulatory institutions and the introduction of a host community development framework were intended to address longstanding structural weaknesses in the industry. He stressed that NNPCL’s commercial autonomy must be matched with corporate accountability, noting that the freedom to make business decisions must come with responsibility for their consequences. Abbas also cautioned against turning legislative oversight into unnecessary interference in the company’s legitimate commercial operations, saying oversight should promote transparency, protect public resources and ensure compliance with statutory responsibilities. He identified crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism, production constraints, infrastructure deficiencies, investment uncertainty and regulatory bottlenecks as major challenges confronting the industry. item.title: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The military has defended its engagement with armed bandits in Kwara State, dismissing allegations of fraternisation with terrorists. They added that the interaction led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The Joint Task Force, Operation Savannah Shield, said the engagement, captured in a video circulating on social media, was part of a security initiative to recover illegal weapons and secure the freedom of abducted persons. In a statement, the task force said the interaction involving military personnel, Department of State Services (DSS) operatives and the armed bandits should not be misconstrued as a compromise of the Armed Forces’ responsibilities. The statement, signed by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu, said the armed elements had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and release their captives. Shittu said the development followed sustained military operations that had put the bandits under intense pressure, leaving them with the options of surrendering or being neutralised. He said the engagement resulted in the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The task force described the outcome as evidence of the effectiveness of its non-kinetic approach, which complements ongoing military offensives against terrorism and banditry. It explained that its operational strategy combined military action, intelligence-driven engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address security challenges. The task force added that individuals willing to surrender would undergo appropriate security screening and other applicable legal procedures. Shittu also said surrendered combatants must not be harmed at the point of surrender, in line with the Law of Armed Conflict, international best practices and established rules of engagement. He stressed that accepting the surrender of armed elements was a recognised and legitimate military outcome, not an indication of unprofessional conduct or compromise. The task force reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting lives and property. It urged members of the public to disregard what it described as misleading interpretations of the video and avoid spreading unverified information capable of undermining ongoing security operations. Operation Savannah Shield assured Nigerians that it would continue to provide updates on its activities through its official communication channels. item.title: Army commissions 20 transit flats, officers’ mess in Bauchi
item.description: By Henry Obetta The Nigerian Army has commissioned 20 transit flats and a modern officers’ mess at Obienu Barracks, Bauchi State, as part of efforts to improve personnel welfare, boost troops’ morale and enhance operational effectiveness. The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, who commissioned the facilities on Wednesday, said the Army’s modernisation drive went beyond the acquisition of military equipment to include improved accommodation, infrastructure and welfare for personnel and their families. According to a statement by the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, Shaibu described decent accommodation and a conducive living environment as critical to troops’ morale, family stability and operational readiness. He explained that the 20 transit flats were designed to address accommodation challenges faced by personnel posted to the barracks for assignments, military courses and other temporary engagements. The COAS said the newly constructed officers’ mess, named the Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu Officers’ Mess, featured modern accommodation, a Hall of Fame and recreational facilities to promote professional interaction, esprit de corps and institutional pride among officers. He commended the Nigerian Army Armoured Corps and other stakeholders for the successful completion of the projects, describing them as evidence of the Army’s commitment to personnel welfare and prudent management of resources. Shaibu urged personnel to ensure proper maintenance of the facilities to guarantee their sustainability and continued usefulness. Reaffirming his commitment to the welfare of troops and their families, the Army chief said investments in accommodation, healthcare, education and other welfare programmes would continue alongside the force’s expansion and modernisation efforts. He stressed that a well-motivated, professionally trained and adequately supported force was essential to sustaining operational successes against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other security threats facing the country. item.title: Tinubu’s economic gains bypass ordinary Nigerians, Makinde campaign tells Alake
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has faulted the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, over his defence of President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the reforms have delivered gains for government institutions and corporate interests but little relief to ordinary Nigerians. The organisation said increased federation revenue, foreign exchange reforms and the clearance of outstanding foreign exchange obligations had not translated into better living conditions, as millions of Nigerians continued to struggle with rising food prices, transportation costs, electricity tariffs and school fees. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the organisation was responding to Alake’s challenge to Nigerians to name any civilian administration that had achieved more across the socio-economic and political spectrum within three years or identify a viable alternative to Tinubu’s economic reforms introduced in May 2023. Ihediwa accused the minister of measuring economic progress through macroeconomic and institutional adjustments while overlooking the daily struggles of ordinary Nigerians. “For the average Nigerian, prosperity was not shared; austerity was distributed universally,” he said. While acknowledging that previous administrations lacked the political will to remove petrol subsidy and unify the exchange rate, the campaign organisation faulted Tinubu for implementing the reforms simultaneously without adequate social protection measures. It argued that combining subsidy removal with currency devaluation and electricity tariff increases imposed multiple economic shocks on households without sufficient measures to cushion their effects. “Taking the bullet is admirable only if you protect the citizens standing behind you,” Ihediwa said. On petrol subsidy removal, the organisation agreed that the previous arrangement was unsustainable and vulnerable to corruption but argued that the government should have provided mass transit alternatives, strengthened domestic refining capacity and introduced effective measures to contain transportation costs before or alongside the policy. It also questioned Alake’s description of the clearance of $7 billion in foreign exchange backlogs and restoration of international card transactions as benefits of exchange rate unification. According to Ihediwa, those gains primarily addressed the concerns of foreign investors, multinational companies and corporate institutions, rather than the immediate needs of Nigerians struggling with the cost of living. He argued that celebrating improved corporate foreign exchange liquidity while local manufacturers battled high borrowing costs and exchange rate volatility reflected a disconnect between the government’s economic priorities and the realities of citizens. item.title: Explosion heard in Riyadh, Saudi capital; missiles intercepted
item.description: A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents said, as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis pressed their campaign of attacks against the kingdom. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis also said they intercepted two cruise missiles — the latest in weeks of strikes targeting military, civilian and oil infrastructure. Later on Wednesday, the coalition said it had intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis in the Riyadh and southern regions, after Saudi authorities had issued and later lifted an alert for the southern Sharurah governorate. Residents said Wednesday’s explosion came without warning, with no mobile-phone alert issued beforehand as is usually the case during aerial threats. “The explosion was extremely loud,” said a resident in northern Riyadh. “Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening.” An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out. The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh’s airport in the northeast of the city. In October, a deadly attack targeting Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed 14 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of flights for two weeks. Within minutes, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the group towards the Riyadh region. Earlier, the coalition had reported intercepting another cruise missile also heading for the same region. Saudi civil defence authorities also said they had activated early warning systems in the southern regions of Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, near the Yemeni border. The Saudi-led coalition, which backs neighbouring Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its war with the Houthis, has battled a surge in attacks since hostilities reignited in July. The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, had been largely dormant after a ceasefire went into effect in 2022. The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the government’s interim capital, having made sweeping territorial gains since the war resumed. Since the summer, more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced by the fighting, according to the United Nations. item.title: Police tighten security for Tinubu rally, Obi visit
item.description: The Anambra State Police Command has intensified security operations across the state ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign rally in Awka and a town hall meeting by the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, in Onitsha. The two political engagements are scheduled for Thursday and Friday, respectively, as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Anambra State Presidential Campaign Council for Tinubu’s re-election is scheduled to hold a mega rally tagged “SoluTinubu 2027” on Thursday, November 19, at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka. Obi, a former governor of the state, is expected to hold a town hall meeting with residents at 2pm on Friday, November 20, at the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha. In a statement on Wednesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, said the command had strengthened patrols, surveillance and personnel deployment in collaboration with other security agencies to ensure peaceful conduct of the events. He said the measures were aimed at preventing criminal activities, maintaining public order and protecting residents, visitors and participants before, during and after the political engagements. According to him, the command has strengthened operational coordination with sister security agencies, area commands, divisions and tactical units to provide adequate security coverage of strategic locations, public facilities, major roads and identified security flashpoints. The statement said the security arrangements also included enhanced intelligence gathering and improved response capabilities to address emerging threats. The Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Ama, was said to have directed operational commanders and personnel to remain vigilant, proactive and professional in the discharge of their duties. Ama also emphasised that security operations must respect human rights and ensure that residents’ movements, businesses and other lawful activities were not unnecessarily disrupted. The command cautioned members of the public, particularly social media users, against inflammatory publications, provocative statements and deliberate dissemination of false information capable of inciting violence or threatening public peace. It, however, acknowledged citizens’ constitutional rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and lawful public engagement, urging individuals and groups to exercise such rights responsibly. “The police will take appropriate lawful measures against individuals whose actions constitute criminal offences, while ensuring that all enforcement activities are guided by due process, professionalism and respect for constitutionally guaranteed rights,” Ikenga said. The command reassured residents, visitors and other members of the public of its commitment to providing a safe environment throughout the period of the scheduled activities. item.title: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign appearances to 19 states, FCT
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has expanded his planned appearances at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rallies from 12 states to 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The revised campaign timetable lists 20 locations where the president is expected to attend rallies between October 24, 2026, and January 13, 2027, according to TheCable, which reported that the schedule was released by APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka. The revised itinerary adds Katsina, Taraba, Abuja, Gusau, Owerri and Ilorin to the president’s initial campaign trail, while also incorporating Akwa Ibom, Jigawa and Kebbi, where he has already attended rallies. Tinubu was initially scheduled to attend rallies in only 12 states, with other party leaders expected to represent him at campaign events in the remaining states. However, he has made appearances in several states outside the original schedule. On November 6, the president visited Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where he attended an APC rally and inaugurated projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration. He followed this with a campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, on November 7. Tinubu also attended the party’s rallies in Dutse, Jigawa State, on November 10, and Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, on November 17. The revised timetable now formally includes the three states among the locations for his personal campaign appearances. Under the updated schedule, Tinubu is expected to attend rallies in Katsina on December 2, Kano on December 17, Jalingo on December 19, Abuja on December 21, Gusau on December 28 and Owerri on December 30. The president is also scheduled to visit Yola, Adamawa State, on January 4; Sokoto on January 5; Ilorin, Kwara State, on January 8; Asaba, Delta State, on January 11; and Lagos on January 13. Other states listed for his personal appearances include Kaduna, Oyo, Borno and Enugu. The revised timetable also changes the dates of some rallies in the original calendar. The Bauchi rally, initially scheduled for November 29 with Tinubu expected to attend, has been moved to December 1, although the new timetable does not indicate a presidential appearance. The Sokoto rally has been shifted from December 5 to January 5, 2027, while the Asaba rally moves from December 12 to January 11. The Lagos rally, expected to serve as the campaign’s major closing event, has also been rescheduled from January 9 to January 13. The updated calendar lists 37 rallies across the 36 states and the FCT, with Tinubu expected to personally attend 20 of them. The North-West has the highest number of states on the president’s revised campaign itinerary, with seven: Kaduna, Jigawa, Kebbi, Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto. The North-East and South-South follow with three states each. The North-East states are Borno, Taraba and Adamawa, while the South-South states are Akwa Ibom, Rivers and Delta. item.title: Senate passes bills establishing research fund, granting medical college PhD powers
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed two bills seeking to provide a framework for research funding and expand postgraduate medical education in Nigeria. The bills are the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill, 2026, and the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, 2026. Both bills were passed on Wednesday after consideration of their provisions, clause by clause, at the Committee of the Whole and subsequent third reading. Their passage followed the presentation and consideration of reports by the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, chaired by Senator Mohammed Dandutse (APC, Katsina South). Presenting the reports, Dandutse said the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill sought to establish a sustainable funding mechanism for research, development and innovation across the country. He said the proposed legislation also provided for the establishment of the National Council on Research and Innovation, which would provide strategic direction, policy oversight and supervision for Nigeria’s research agenda. According to him, the proposed fund would support research institutions and provide a dedicated funding framework for addressing the country’s development challenges. He added that the fund and the council would work together to strengthen Nigeria’s research, scientific, technological and innovation capabilities. On the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, Dandutse said the proposed amendment sought to expand the academic and institutional functions of the college. He explained that the amendment would empower the college to establish academic programmes and award Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in specialised medical disciplines. The areas include clinical medicine, dentistry, basic medical sciences, pharmacology and other related fields. Dandutse further explained that the amendment would empower the college’s Senate to develop, administer and supervise the proposed doctoral programmes. He said the programmes would be subject to accreditation and regulation by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to ensure compliance with prescribed academic standards. According to him, the proposed changes are intended to provide a framework for advanced medical education, clinical research and specialised medical training in the country. item.title: World Bank threatened to cut Nigeria’s financing over subsidy — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has said the World Bank warned Nigeria that it would stop financing the country unless the Federal Government removed petrol subsidy. Fashola, who served as Minister of Power under the late President Muhammadu Buhari, made the disclosure on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He said the decision to remove the subsidy was not merely a policy choice, but was also influenced by legal provisions and Nigeria’s financial position at the time. Fashola urged Nigerians to revisit President Bola Tinubu’s inaugural address, arguing that public attention had focused largely on the declaration that “subsidy is gone” without sufficient consideration of other parts of the speech. He also cited the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), which he said provided for petroleum products to be sold at competitive market rates, arguing that the provision had implications for any move to reinstate subsidy. “The World Bank simply said, ‘We won’t finance your country again unless you remove subsidy.’ It was that simple,” he said. Fashola said the issue had been discussed during the previous administration, when he was a member of the Federal Executive Council, adding that Nigeria was spending close to 90 per cent of its revenue on debt servicing. He argued that the country could not afford to sustain the subsidy regime and challenged those advocating its restoration to explain how they intended to fund it. The former minister also asked political opponents of the Tinubu administration to explain how they would implement an alternative policy if elected, saying some politicians who had previously supported subsidy removal had changed their positions after it became unpopular. He said the Tinubu administration deserved commendation for maintaining the policy despite the economic difficulties it had imposed on Nigerians. “What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on its word and saying, ‘Because the people like it, let’s bring it back.’ It was a road to perdition,” he said. Fashola, however, acknowledged that subsidy removal had affected household livelihoods and increased the cost of living, but said the government was introducing other measures to cushion the impact. He listed tax reforms, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), salary adjustments and compressed natural gas (CNG) initiatives among the measures being deployed to address the economic pressures. He also cited a decline in inflation from above 30 per cent to about 14 per cent, arguing that reversing the subsidy policy midway could disrupt the progress recorded. The former governor recalled the Subsidy Reinvestment and Empowerment Programme (SURE-P), introduced under former President Goodluck Jonathan, as an earlier attempt to manage the proceeds from subsidy removal. item.title: DSS challenges Atiku to prove it recruited protesters in Sokoto
item.description: …Says preliminary investigation found no evidence against operatives …Recalls rescuing ADC governorship candidate from attack The Department of State Services (DSS) has challenged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to provide concrete evidence to support his allegation that the agency recruited protesters to disrupt the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign rally in Sokoto State. The secret police said its preliminary investigation into the allegation failed to establish any evidence linking its operatives to the organisation or sponsorship of protests against the ADC’s campaign activities in the state. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, had earlier accused the Sokoto State Government of obstructing his party’s campaign activities ahead of its rally in the state. Addressing journalists in Abuja, the former Vice-President also alleged that the DSS recruited protesters to cause unrest and create grounds for imposing a curfew that could prevent the opposition party from holding its rally as scheduled. However, in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Deputy Director of Public Relations and Strategic Communications of the DSS, Favour Dozie, said the agency activated its internal investigation procedures following the public allegation. Dozie said the investigation was conducted on the directive of the Director-General of the DSS, Adeola Ajayi, and involved interviews with ADC leaders in Sokoto, party members and other relevant stakeholders. According to the spokesperson, Atiku had specifically alleged that the ADC knew where some of the protesters were assembled and how they were allegedly deployed to strategic locations. Quoting the former Vice-President, Dozie said: “Where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout.” The DSS spokesperson, however, said the agency’s preliminary findings did not substantiate the allegation. “Outcome of the preliminary investigation did not confirm the allegation, as there was no evidence to establish such,” the statement said. In presenting its account of its activities in Sokoto, the agency recalled that on October 31, its operatives rescued Mannir Daniya, the ADC governorship candidate in the state, from an attack and evacuated him to safety. It said two of its operatives were assaulted during the rescue operation and were receiving medical attention at the time of its earlier statement. The agency further disclosed that Daniya subsequently contacted the State Director of the DSS to express appreciation for the intervention and request additional security reinforcement. It also said it received letters of appreciation from the ADC state chairman and the governorship candidate, describing the correspondence as evidence of its efforts to protect political actors irrespective of their party affiliations. item.title: Atiku questions Tinubu’s Villa interview over $4.5m US lobbying deal
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has questioned whether President Bola Tinubu’s recently recorded interview at the Presidential Villa was connected to a $4.5 million lobbying contract involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Atiku demanded that the Presidency disclose the terms of the contract, explain the purpose of the payment and release the full, unedited interview to establish whether the recording was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. In a statement on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified Diana London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged to work for the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings showed that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but did not establish whether the presidential interview was covered by the contract. Atiku also criticised the Presidency for presenting the recorded encounter as an interview while promoting it with photographs and a ‘coming soon’ announcement. “When Tinubu is ready for an interview, he should let Nigerians know. He cannot invite a strategist registered to work for his government, record a publicity production and advertise Sitting on a Flat Mandate as ‘coming soon’, like a trailer from 51 Iweka Road, Onitsha. “Hungry Nigerians are not here to market his failed movie. They have suffered through Part One of Tinubu’s government, and they will not sit through a sequel,” he said. The former vice president also questioned London’s professional relationship with the lobbying firm and her decision to delete social media posts in which she had praised Tinubu’s administration and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States. “After praising Tinubu’s government and Nigeria’s partnership with the United States on her social media accounts, Diana London deleted the posts. She has not explained why. Nigerians are entitled to ask what changed between the glowing praise and its disappearance,” Atiku said. He argued that the deleted posts and questions surrounding London’s professional engagements reinforced the need for the Presidency to release the complete recording. “Someone who could delete her own public praise of this government without an explanation has given Nigerians reason to wonder what will survive the editing of her interview. Will difficult questions and awkward answers remain in the final cut? Or will Nigerians be served a carefully redacted, defensive account that mutilates the facts? The Presidency can put those doubts to rest by releasing the full, unedited recording,” he said. item.title: NELFUND: I dare opposition to promise scrapping scheme — Fashola
item.description: …Says students, beneficiaries would revolt against such proposal Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged opposition politicians to campaign on a promise to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying beneficiaries and their families would resist such a move. Fashola, who spoke on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, described the student loan scheme introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration as one of the reforms that had eased the financial burden on families across the country. NELFUND was established in April 2024 after Tinubu signed the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act into law to provide interest-free loans to eligible students in tertiary institutions. As of October 3, 2026, the fund said it had disbursed more than ₦372 billion to 1,635,676 beneficiaries across 312 tertiary institutions nationwide. Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Jigawa on November 10, Tinubu had described NELFUND as a weapon deployed by his administration to tackle poverty, insisting that the scheme would not be discontinued. Supporting the President’s position, Fashola said the initiative was introduced to help Nigerian families cope with financial obligations, particularly rent, transportation, healthcare and education. “This led to the creation of NELFUND to help families pay school fees and provide student allowances,” he said. He noted that more than one million Nigerians were already benefiting from the scheme, adding that the number was increasing. Fashola challenged opposition candidates to make the discontinuation of the programme part of their campaign promises, saying such a position would attract resistance from beneficiaries and their families. “I challenge the opponents to promise to scrap NELFUND and see how beneficiaries and their families react. They won’t dare,” he said. The former Minister of Works and Housing also addressed the rising cost of living, describing it as a global challenge whose effects were being felt in Nigeria. He called for a broader understanding of the factors contributing to the economic hardship, pointing to disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent global developments. According to him, the pandemic disrupted economic activities worldwide, forcing governments to inject money into their economies to support businesses. He said China, which he described as the world’s biggest production centre, took about two to three years to resume normal operations, contributing to supply shortages and rising prices. Fashola also identified the Russia-Ukraine war as another factor that worsened the situation, citing disruptions to the supply of energy products, including diesel, and food commodities such as wheat. item.title: ADC, Kaduna gov’t differ over venue
item.description: From Mohammed Ibrahim Yaba, Kaduna; Hussein Yahaya, Baba Martins & Daniel Adaji, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Kaduna State Government of denying the party the use of the Ranchers Bees Stadium to host the Northwest rally of its presidential campaign. The party said it had applied to use the stadium for its rally scheduled for November 17 and 18 but was refused access to the facility by the state government, which denied the claim. The ADC National Vice Chairman, North-West, Hafsat Baba, told one of our correspondents that the party dutifully informed the state government of its intention to use the facility, but the latter turned down its request. Daily Trust reports that the All Progressives Congress (APC) recently held its presidential campaign flag-off at the same venue. In a letter dated November 12, 2026 reportedly from the Kaduna State Ministry of Local Government Affairs and addressed to the Office of the National Vice Chairman of the ADC, North-West, the ministry said the stadium would not be available on the requested dates due to ongoing repairs. The letter, signed by Mohammed Sani Haruna, Senior Special Assistant to the Commissioner, stated: “We write to acknowledge receipt of your letter with the above caption. However, we regret to inform you that due to ongoing repairs at the stadium, it will not be available for the aforementioned programme on the dates requested by you.” Baba said the ADC also notified security agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Inspector-General of Police, Kaduna State Police Command and the General Officer Commanding, about the planned rally. “We sent these letters not only to state security agencies but also to their national offices, just to be on the safe side,” she said. Baba explained that the party initially considered the Ahmadu Bello Stadium but was informed that it was under construction and subsequently considered the Trade Fair Complex but was also told that the facility would not be available. She said the party decided to request Ranchers Bees Stadium after learning that the APC had recently used it for its presidential campaign flag-off. “We were aware that Ahmadu Bello Stadium was under construction. We then thought of using the Trade Fair Complex, but we were made to understand that it would also not be available. We knew that they (APC) used Ranchers Bees recently, so we decided to request it, but it was denied,” she said. The ADC chieftain questioned why its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, should be prevented from holding a rally in Kaduna, which she described as his second home. “If Atiku can visit Bauchi and Yobe and hold his rallies, why can’t he come to Kaduna, his second home, because he has a house here?” she asked. item.title: Gaming Phenomenon ‘Grand Theft Auto’ Goes Live After 13-Year Wait
item.description: After 13 years of waiting, including two delays and several leaks, the first gamers began playing Wednesday the latest instalment of “Grand Theft Auto”, the most expensive — and among the most profitable — video game ever developed. “GTA VI” becomes available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at midnight Thursday in each region where it will be available. That meant it launched first in New Zealand (at 1100 GMT on Wednesday), with many players around the world changing their console location settings to the far-eastern country to be among the first to enter the new Vice City. “I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time that the anticipation for this is crazy,” Australian student Riley Fennel told AFP ahead of the launch. Although Rockstar Games, the studio behind GTA, has not yet released advance unit sales figures, specialist firm Sensor Tower estimates they have already surpassed 15 million. That would be more than $1.5 billion in revenue before the game even came out, for a budget estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion, which would be unprecedented. According to the British analytics firm Omdia, sales of “GTA VI” could reach $3.2 billion by the end of the year. An organiser fixes a poster of the video game ‘Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI’ ahead of its launch party in Chennai on November 17, 2026. Photo by R.SATISH BABU / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ “No other concert or box office release has ever generated that much capital. And so that makes it one of the outliers in entertainment,” said Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” the industry specialist said. Rockstar’s parent company, US publisher Take-Two Interactive, has rolled out a massive marketing campaign to establish the title as a mass cultural product that transcends the boundaries of video games. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said James McWhirter at Omdia. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning this first game session “for a very long time”. Like him, many fans have already booked time off to immerse themselves in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida. The human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests around the world for November 19. Touted as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows the adventures of a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in the Miami-inspired, crime-ravaged Vice City. Since its beginnings, the series has won players over with its increasingly realistic reconstructions of fictionalised cities and the great freedom of action offered in a highly detailed open world. item.title: State Police: Senate Directs NASS Clerk To Transmit Amendment Bill To Tinubu For Assent
item.description: The Senate has directed the clerk to the National Assembly to transmit the Constitution alteration bill providing for the establishment of State Police to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The upper chamber has also asked the Executive to forward the National Policing Bill to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage to establish the operational framework for subnational policing. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, during plenary today. Policemen at the Niger State Police Command (Photo by Abdullahi Egba/Channels TV) In its deliberations, Senator Bamidele recalled that the National Assembly had processed an executive bill seeking to amend the 1999 Constitution to establish state police as part of Nigeria’s national policing structure. He noted that both chambers overwhelmingly approved the proposed amendment, with the Senate passing the bill on June 24, 2026, and the House of Representatives following suit on July 23, 2026, securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority. The bill was subsequently transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for approval in line with Section 9(2) of the Constitution. The Senate Leader noted that the Senate confirmed that all 36 state legislatures had now endorsed the proposed amendment and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly. Having satisfied the constitutional requirements under Sections 9(1) and 9(2), the Senate maintained that the amendment had fulfilled the conditions necessary for its passage. The upper chamber therefore urged the Executive to submit the National Policing Bill to provide the legal and operational framework for the implementation of State Police. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced on Monday that all 36 State Houses of Assembly had approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, clearing the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The clerk described it as 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures, as the approval exceeded the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. “The Clerk to the National Assembly wishes to announce that all the thirty-six (36) State Houses of Assembly have approved ‘A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for related Matters’. “This represents one hundred percent (100%) endorsement by the State Houses of Assembly, which exceeds the threshold of twenty-four (24), provided under Section 9(2) of the Constitution (as amended),” Ogunlana had stated. The development marked the completion of the state assemblies’ consideration of the proposed amendment, following weeks of legislative engagement over the establishment of state police.
